claim.markdown_says: `## 15.3.3.3 ...`, `## 15.3.3.4 Local time formats`, `## 15.3.3.5 UTC time formats`, `## 15.3.3.6 Offset time formats`, `## 15.3.3.6.1 Offset subformats` (all level 2), whereas siblings `### 15.3.3.1 Common time formats with integer seconds representation` and `### 15.3.3.2 Common time formats with fractional seconds representation` (page 831) and `### 15.3.3.6.2 Permissible values for data associated with offset time formats` (page 833) are level 3
claim.why_it_matters: Same defect as page 830 and additionally one level deeper: 15.3.3.6.1 is emitted at level 2 while its own sibling 15.3.3.6.2 is at level 3, so the two halves of the offset-subformat specification end up at different depths and 15.3.3.6.1 detaches from 15.3.3.6.

verdict.reasoning: I attempted to refute this on every available ground and could not. (1) Both quotations are accurate. The 300dpi render of PDF page 832 (printed folio 802) shows exactly five bold numbered headings, in order, with the titles as claimed: '15.3.3.3 Permissible values for data associated with common time formats', '15.3.3.4 Local time formats', '15.3.3.5 UTC time formats', '15.3.3.6 Offset time formats', '15.3.3.6.1 Offset subformats'. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 33566, 33577, 33582, 33587 and 33594 emit all five with a two-hash prefix. (2) The sibling levels are as claimed: lines 33534 and 33541 emit '### 15.3.3.1' and '### 15.3.3.2', and line 33630 emits '### 15.3.3.6.2' -- level 3. Line 33531 emits the parent '## 15.3.3 Common time formats' at level 2 and line 33641 emits '### 15.3.3.7 Combined date and time formats' at level 3. So the enclosing subtree establishes the convention unambiguously: 15.3.3 is level 2 and its .N children are level 3, and the transcription honours that for .1, .2 and .7 while breaking it for .3 through .6. (3) This is NOT dismissable as mere formatting. The markdown contradicts itself between DIRECT siblings: 15.3.3.6.1 sits at level 2 and 15.3.3.6.2 at level 3, and the file's own treatment of that five-component depth (line 33630) proves level 3 is what it intends there. Whatever convention one prefers, no convention can place a section and its immediate sibling at different depths, nor place a child (15.3.3.6.1) at the same level as its own parent (15.3.3.6). Under the emitted levels 15.3.3.6.1 is a PEER of 15.3.3.6 rather than contained by it, which is a false containment relationship, not a rendering nicety -- it corrupts TOC nesting and any tooling that derives section hierarchy from heading depth. (4) I checked for the usual escape hatches and found none: nothing is reflowed onto an adjacent line, there is no hyphenation or page-break furniture involved, and no heading text is lost or altered. (5) I separately verified that the prose on page 832 is transcribed faithfully, so the heading levels are the only defect: the asymmetric wording of the two LEAP-SECOND sentences is correctly preserved ('greater than or equal to 00 and IS less than 60 ... OFF phrase' vs 'greater than or equal to 00 and less than 61 ... ON phrase'), as are the trailing semicolon in 'one of the following values;' and 'adjusted downward by the offset values to represent UTC;'. Page 832 both begins and ends where the markdown says it does (heading 15.3.3.3 through enumerated item 1). Confirmed.
verdict.corrected_description: The finding is real and the claim describes it accurately. Two refinements. First, on the intended levels: the enclosing subtree fixes the convention as 15.3.3 = level 2 with its .N children = level 3 (honoured at 15.3.3.1, 15.3.3.2 and 15.3.3.7), so 15.3.3.3 through 15.3.3.6 should each be level 3; for 15.3.3.6.1 the transcription's own handling of its sibling 15.3.3.6.2 at line 33630 sets level 3 as the file's local convention for that depth, so 15.3.3.6.1 should be level 3 to match it (a strictly depth-proportional scheme would want level 4, but matching 15.3.3.6.2 is what makes the pair self-consistent). Second, and more important for the fix: this is NOT page-832-local, so a five-heading patch would leave the pattern alive. The identical demotion runs through the preceding sibling group on pages 830-831 -- '## 15.3.1.5 Permissible values for data associated with ordinal date formats' (line 33489), '## 15.3.1.6 Week date formats' (33496) and '## 15.3.1.7 Permissible values for data associated with week date formats' (33503) are level 2 while their siblings 15.3.1.1 through 15.3.1.4 (lines 33443, 33458, 33465, 33474) are level 3. Worse, the subtree root is inverted: '### 15.3 Arguments' (line 33366) is emitted DEEPER than its own child '## 15.3.1 Format arguments to international date and time functions' (line 33440). In every instance the demotion begins at the heading that follows a general-format diagram or a table, which points at a single root cause in the heading-level assignment pass rather than a set of independent slips. The remediation should be a re-level of the whole 15.3 subtree, root included, verified against the numeric depth of each heading.
